title: Same piece first, then the tops add

interactive.brief: The one thing you should see is the 1/2 run gain a cut and read 2/4, so the two counts, 2 and 3, add to the 5 quarters the joined run shows, when you count both in quarters.
interactive.title: Count both, then add
interactive.whatAmILookingAt: Two one-hour bars with runs of 1/2 and 3/4, joined or taken away. The stepper picks the piece; the counts then add or subtract. New top = top × (new bottom ÷ old bottom).
interactive.ignores: Only pieces that measure both are offered; halves or sixths would not measure 3/4 exactly.

explain.text:
Fractions add only once they count the same piece.[^1] Half an hour plus three-quarters: 1/2 is 2/4, so 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4, an hour and a quarter, 75 minutes. Add the tops and keep the bottom.[^2] Taking away works the same: 3/4 − 2/4 = 1/4, 15 minutes.[^3]

The trap is adding top and bottom: 1/2 + 3/4 = 4/6. That is 40 minutes, less than the 45 you started with.

**Match the piece, then add the tops and keep the bottom: 1/2 + 3/4 = 5/4.**

analogy.text: You never add 750 mm and 1.5 m as 751.5. Put both in millimetres: 750 + 1500 = 2250 mm.
analogy.breaks: A metre is always 1000 mm; with fractions you choose the piece and check it measures both.

practice.text:
**Rule of thumb:** same piece first; then tops add and the bottom stays.

**Worked example:** visits of 1 3/4 and 2 1/2 hours. 1 + 2 = 3, and 3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4. Total 4 1/4 hours.

**Common mistakes**
- Adding the bottoms: 1/2 + 3/4 as 4/6.
- Adding the tops before matching the piece.

sources.title: Adding and subtracting fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: When you're adding and subtracting fractions with different denominators, you need to change one, and sometimes both, of the fractions so that they have the same denominator.

sources.title: Adding and subtracting fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: When the denominators are the same you can just add the numerators.

sources.title: How to subtract fractions - BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: To find the difference between fractions with the same denominator, subtract the numerators. The denominator remains the same.
